name: slack-thread-to-notion-discussion

deploy.description: Slack -> Notion half of the thread <-> discussion two-way sync. Listens to every public-channel message (instant Slack event subscription; fires on thread replies too — verified by deployed test 2026-09-01). A message in a mapped thread mirrors into the mapped Notion discussion as a comment under the Slack author's own display_name. A message in an unmapped thread that names a ticket (TKT-###) or pastes a Notion page URL links the thread: opens a page-level discussion (joins the newest open page-level thread if the page already has one — API limitation), backfills the thread, and confirms in-thread. Everything else exits at the free guard path.
deploy.note: Never attempted by failed publish run 33483876845 (2026-09-01) — the job died on the sweep before reaching this directory. Touched so the retry merge picks it up.

trigger.trigger_note: Public channels only by design (v1 scope). listen_for_bots is set to no but has proven inconsistent — the workflow body re-checks user.is_bot explicitly, which is also echo-suppression layer 1 for the sync's own Slack posts.
trigger.why_not_polling: Deployed Slack triggers register a Slack event subscription (delivery in seconds). Sample polls never show thread replies — that is documented test-time behaviour, not the deployed behaviour.

description: Slack -> Notion half of the Slack thread <-> Notion discussion two-way sync (TKT-825). Mention a TKT-### (or paste a Notion page URL) in any public Slack thread to link it to that task; from then on every human message in the thread mirrors into the task's Notion discussion, attributed via display_name. Companion Zaps: notion-comment-to-slack-thread (reverse direction) and slack-notion-thread-sync-sweep (resolve detection + self-healing backstop).
